test_title: PYST 29: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - Quant (Held On 02 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Chords AB and CD intersect inside a circle at point O.

If AO = 8 cm, OB = 12 cm, and CO = 6 cm, find OD.

(O is the origin)
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Core logic: For any two chords intersecting inside a circle, the product of the segments of one chord equals the product of the segments of the other chord.

AO × OB = CO × OD

8 × 12 = 6 × OD

96 = 6 × OD ⇒ OD = 16 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

AO = 8 cm

OB = 12 cm

CO = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Intersecting Chords Theorem: If two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at a point O inside the circle, then AO × OB = CO × OD.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a9f3b46454089ce834040536d46ff8e3949aba0f8463a4db6f3f541132b0c6d5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ AO × OB = CO × OD

⇒ 8 × 12 = 6 × OD

⇒ 96 = 6 × OD

⇒ OD = 96 ÷ 6

⇒ OD = 16 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Intersecting Secants Theorem (External)

If two secant segments PAB and PCD are drawn to a circle from an exterior point P, then PA × PB = PC × PD.

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent segment PT and a secant segment PAB are drawn to a circle from an exterior point P, then PT² = PA × PB.

Perpendicular from Center

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.</p
